title: Minimum Reverse Operations
summary: Given an array of length n initialized to zeros with a single 1 at position p, and a banned positions array, reverse subarrays of size k to move the single 1 to each position i, recording the minimum operations needed for each position, or -1 if impossible.
statement: Given an array of length n initialized to zeros with a single 1 at position p, and a banned positions array, reverse subarrays of size k to move the single 1 to each position i, recording the minimum operations needed for each position, or -1 if impossible.
constraints: A length-n binary array has its only one at p; an operation reverses any contiguous length-k subarray.
The one may not land on a banned index.
Return each index's minimum operations from p, using -1 when unreachable.
hints: For one position, valid reversal starts map it to a same-parity interval [low, high].
Breadth-first search supplies minimum operation counts.
Keep unvisited non-banned indices split by parity, with successor disjoint sets that skip indices after removal.
Each reachable index is enqueued and removed once; interval bounds enumerate exactly all one-reversal destinations.
editorial: Each reachable index is enqueued and removed once; interval bounds enumerate exactly all one-reversal destinations.

tests.explanation: Reversing the whole array moves the one from zero to three; banned indices remain unreachable.
Successive length-two reversals move the one one step at a time, giving distances zero through four.
